title: British Empire
capsule: The British Empire in its mid-period (1757–1858) expanded from a commercially driven Atlantic and Indian Ocean network into a territorial empire of unprecedented scale, anchored by the conquest of Bengal following Robert Clive's victory at Plassey in 1757. The Seven Years' War (1756–1763) delivered Canada, several Caribbean islands, and decisive influence in India, while the post-Napoleonic settlement of 1815 added the Cape Colony, Ceylon, Malta, and other strategic nodes. The East India Company administered much of the Indian subcontinent until the Rebellion of 1857, after which the Crown assumed direct rule with the Government of India Act 1858, transforming the Company's domains into the British Raj. At this juncture Britain held roughly a quarter of the world's land surface and dominated global maritime commerce.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial boundaries of British colonial possessions in this period are well documented through Admiralty charts, Colonial Office records, and treaty texts; internal frontier zones in West Africa and parts of Central Asia are approximate, but core territories are precisely attested.
